solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good example of European fashion included in list

indicators.note: included in tells us the European fashion sits inside the word for list

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a class roll
mode means fashion, as in 'all the mode'

explanation.surface: A catalogue of styles features some trend from the Continent as a model to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose conduct sets a good example for others to copy.

clue.text: Starving birds seen around old university

indicators.note: seen around says the birds are placed so as to surround the next letters

parts.note: ravens are large black birds of the crow family

explanation.surface: Hungry birds are spotted circling an ancient college.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means extremely hungry, a synonym of starving.

clue.text: Odd parts of life poorly presented here? Rubbish

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of 'life' are L and F, written out in words as L AND F
poorly means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark: the strange bits of a life told badly, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in 'Odd parts': the odd-numbered letters of 'life' are its first and third, and the setter has them read out as a phrase joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfill is waste buried in the ground at a tip, so the word stands for the rubbish itself.

clue.text: A wife in one African country or another

definitions.note: here means another African country, following on from the one named in the wordplay

indicators.note: in tells us the A and W are placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man's wife lives in some African state, or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'one African country' builds the answer and 'or another' asks for a second African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in southeastern Africa, so it is indeed a further country of that continent.

clue.text: Junior minister involved in trade, a Conservative

indicators.note: involved in says the answer is tucked away inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run on across 'trade, a Conservative'

explanation.surface: A low-ranking government minister with a trade portfolio turns out to be a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' looks political, but here it is a churchman ranking below a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained cleric ranking below a priest, hence a junior minister of the church.

clue.text: Unusually brittle old book

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of brittle are to be arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An ancient volume has become strangely fragile.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera, often called its book, as in 'book and lyrics'.

clue.text: A doctor's letters, perhaps, about one bug

indicators.note: about tells us the doctor's letters surround the numeral

parts.note: PhD is the set of letters after the name of a doctor of philosophy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something a physician has written is perhaps about a single germ.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, and bug is a general word for any such insect.

clue.text: This kind of competition 'asn't 'ealthy effect on people

parts.note: hasn't a healthy effect on means harms; said in the clue's Cockney accent, with every H dropped, it comes out without its H
a race is a people, an ethnic group

explanation.surface: A Cockney grumbles that something is bad for folk's health.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H's of the surface are the instruction: the word for 'hasn't a healthy effect on' is said in the same accent, losing its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An arms race is a contest between powers to build up weapons, a kind of competition.

clue.text: Place that's hot, associated with our home

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Earth is the planet that is home to us all

explanation.surface: A warm spot is linked with the place we live.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth is the floor of a fireplace, the warm spot at the heart of a house.

clue.text: Scientist of note pictured with Queen

definitions.text: Scientist of note pictured with Queen

parts.words: Scientist of note pictured with Queen
parts.note: the naturalist of evolution fame appeared on the Bank of England ten-pound note, opposite the Queen's head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of note' reads as 'famous', but it is literal: the scientist was printed on a banknote alongside the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin, the naturalist behind natural selection, featured on the British ten-pound banknote from 2000.

clue.text: Bland in-house article

indicators.note: in places the article within the word for house

parts.note: a villa is a kind of house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dull item that is made on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-house' reads as one word, but the hyphen hides 'in' as the insertion signal and 'house' as the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used to mean plain or ordinary, without extras, like the most basic ice cream flavour.

clue.text: Some Irish sailors needed to get into port

definitions.text: Some Irish sailors needed to get into port

parts.words: Some Irish sailors needed to get into port
parts.note: the crew of a ship from Cork, an Irish county, might need to reach port, but the port here is the drink, and you need a tool to open its bottle

explanation.walkthrough: Read as CORK'S CREW, sailors from Cork; the port to be got into is the fortified wine, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool that draws the stopper from a wine bottle, so it lets you get at the port.

clue.text: One of the things known by expert about religious belief

indicators.note: about says the vegetable goes round the religious word

parts.words: One of the things known by expert
parts.note: an expert is said to know their onions, so an onion is one of the things known
pi is an informal word for pious or religious

explanation.surface: A specialist's knowledge concerns matters of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know your onions' is a British idiom for being expert in a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or judgement someone holds, a belief not necessarily founded on proof.

clue.text: Money a head cuts for kind of lecture

indicators.note: cuts means the per-person phrase slices into the word for money

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
a head means each, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A fee per person reduces the takings for some sort of talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture and discussion session on a topical issue, popular in 1960s universities.

clue.text: Advance that nobody else can achieve

definitions.text: Advance that nobody else can achieve

parts.words: Advance that nobody else can achieve
parts.note: a kind of progress only you can bring about for yourself

explanation.walkthrough: The 'nobody else' reads as a boast about a unique feat, but it means the progress is something only the person concerned can make for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-improvement is bettering one's own character or skills by one's own efforts.

clue.text: It's not altogether evident if you are empathetic

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase, matching the verb as used with 'you'

indicators.note: not altogether says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across 'evident if you'

explanation.surface: Your empathy is only partly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify with someone is to share their feelings, which is what being empathetic involves.

clue.text: With piano, is including pieces for playing without compassion

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: including says the word is wraps round the playing pieces

parts.note: tiles are the playing pieces in games such as Scrabble and mahjong

explanation.surface: A pianist taking in pieces to perform plays heartlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces for playing' suggests music to go with the piano, but they are game tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiless means showing no pity or mercy, so lacking any compassion.

clue.text: No fast food for French gourmet

definitions.text: No fast food for French gourmet

parts.words: No fast food for French gourmet
parts.note: a delicacy prized in French cuisine that comes from a famously slow creature, so it is anything but fast food

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a gourmet scorning burgers; the joke is that the dish is literally slow, a snail.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French culinary name for edible snails, notoriously sluggish animals.

clue.text: Person leaving cricket match at Oval before end of over

indicators.note: before puts the oval shape ahead of the next letter

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
O is oval in shape

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of over

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a Test at the Oval before the over is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, so 'Oval' looks like a venue but only supplies its O shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, someone leaving property to heirs.

clue.text: Position of responsibility prophet's accepting time and time again

indicators.note: accepting says the prophet takes the time abbreviation into himself

parts.note: Hosea is an Old Testament prophet; the 's means 'prophet is'
again means time once more, a second T

explanation.surface: A prophet keeps taking on a role with heavy duties, over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot seat is the uncomfortable position of someone who must take decisions and face criticism.

clue.text: Head off rabbit or hare's companion

indicators.note: head off tells us to lose the first letter of the word for rabbit

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk

explanation.surface: Something removes the head of a rabbit or a hare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' and 'hare' paint an animal scene, but rabbit is a verb meaning to talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hatter is the March Hare's tea-party companion in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Breaking end of pot, a kind of porcelain

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of pot

parts.note: Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Smashing the base of a precious Ming vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' sits with pot and porcelain as smashing, but here it means taming, as in breaking a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a horse is to train it to accept a rider, which is taming it.

clue.text: Men engaged in monetary arrangements omitting first name

indicators.note: omitting says a letter is left out of the money word

parts.note: finances are money matters and arrangements

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of name

explanation.surface: Men involved in financial deals leave out their forename.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' looks like a phrase, but 'Men engaged' is the definition and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man engaged to be married, so fiancés are such men.

clue.text: Not welcoming American poet unknown here

parts.note: Robert Frost was an American poet
Y is an algebraic unknown, as are X and Z

explanation.surface: A US poet here is not recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty reception is a cold, unfriendly one, the opposite of welcoming.

clue.text: Turn up in a first part of press conference, for example

indicators.note: first part of picks the opening letter of press

parts.note: Conference is a variety of pear

explanation.surface: Show up at a press briefing, say.
explanation.walkthrough: A press conference seems one phrase, but 'press' gives a letter and Conference is a British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to arrive or show up, the same as to turn up.

clue.text: Mother goes in to cultivate old fruit

indicators.note: goes in says the mother word is placed inside the words that follow

parts.note: to till is to cultivate the soil
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum goes off to tend some old-fashioned fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green husk-covered fruit used in Mexican cooking, related to the Cape gooseberry.

clue.text: Deception or heartless lie, in a sense

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened lie goes inside the sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

indicators.note: heartless means removing the middle letter of lie, leaving its outside

explanation.surface: A trick, or a cruel untruth, in some sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity used to deceive, as in sleight of hand, so it means trickery.

clue.text: Gem of a girl embracing good sport

indicators.note: embracing says the girl's name wraps round the letter for good

parts.note: Ruby is both a gem and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lovely girl is hugging a good sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a football game played with an oval ball, a sport.

clue.text: Adman whose work is highly regarded

definitions.text: Adman whose work is highly regarded

parts.words: Adman whose work is highly regarded
parts.note: an advertiser whose messages are written high up, so they are literally regarded, looked at, aloft

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly regarded' means esteemed in the surface, but literally means looked at up high.
explanation.definitionFit: A skywriter is a pilot tracing advertising messages in smoke across the sky.
